chunks.subject: AP European History
chunks.title: DBQ — Document-Based Question (7 points) — Set 1: French Revolutionary Government
chunks.content: AP European History DBQ, 7 points, standardized rubric. A Thesis/Claim [1]: a historically defensible thesis/claim that responds to the prompt with a line of reasoning (in the intro or conclusion; not a restatement). B Contextualization [1]: describes a broader historical context relevant to the prompt. C Evidence [0–3]: (1) uses the content of at least THREE documents to address the topic; (1) supports an argument in response to the prompt using at least FOUR documents; (1) uses at least one additional piece of specific historical evidence BEYOND the documents. D Analysis and Reasoning [0–2]: (1) Sourcing — explains for at least TWO documents how the point of view, purpose, historical situation, and/or audience is relevant to an argument; (1) Complex Understanding — demonstrates a complex understanding via sophisticated argumentation and/or effective use of evidence (e.g., corroboration/qualification, argument + counterargument across all documents). Set 1 prompt: evaluate the extent to which the French revolutionary government upheld the ideals of the French Revolution (7 documents). Common failure: using only three documents (loses the four-document argument point), no sourcing attempt, and evidence-beyond-the-documents that is too vague.

chunks.subject: AP European History
chunks.title: DBQ Set 1 exemplar — Sample 1A, 7/7
chunks.content: DBQ (Set 1) scored 7/7 (Thesis 1, Context 1, Evidence 3, Analysis 2). Thesis linking the government's granting of rights to subduing revolutionary spirit; contextualization via excessive spending and unfair taxation; used all seven documents (3-doc and 4-doc argument points) plus evidence beyond (conditions of slavery); sourced four documents (audience for Docs 4 and 7, purpose for Docs 5 and 6); complex understanding via an argument-and-counterargument using all seven documents. Full-credit model.

chunks.subject: AP European History
chunks.title: DBQ Set 1 exemplar — Sample 1B, 4/7
chunks.content: DBQ (Set 1) scored 4/7 (Thesis 1, Context 1, Evidence 2, Analysis 0). Earned the thesis (government did not live up to the ideals), contextualization (Enlightenment ideas, American independence), the 3-document content point, and evidence beyond the documents (actions of the Jacobins). Lost the 4-document argument point (used only 3 documents), and both Analysis points — no sourcing attempt and no complex understanding. Illustrates the common ceiling: solid thesis/context/evidence but no document sourcing or complexity.

chunks.subject: AP European History
chunks.title: DBQ Set 1 exemplar — Sample 1C, 2/7
chunks.content: DBQ (Set 1) scored 2/7 (Thesis 1, Context 1, Evidence 0, Analysis 0). Earned only the thesis (government upheld the ideals by granting rights) and contextualization (Old Regime inequalities, American Revolution). Lost all evidence points (referenced only two documents, so neither the 3-doc nor 4-doc point; evidence beyond was too vague) and both Analysis points. Illustrates a response that frames an argument but does not deploy enough document evidence.
